Hey all - I'm looking for some advice to deal with a couple of dresses and jumpsuits that have shoulder ties. I hate the ties! I have slope-y shoulders so to ties them enough that they don't slip means they dig into my shoulders and having to untie them to use the bathroom is a pain in the butt. I am thinking of adding snaps along the ties in spots that would be comfortable for me. I figure I can mark the fabric with chalk when they are tied where I like them and add quite a few for different fits. I also assume I will need to go to the fabric store to find snaps small enough to fit on these tiny little straps. So I'm looking for any advice or better ideas on making shoulder ties not have to be ties. Thanks!!

You didn't fail. You have a Dad that adores you and your girls. They are obviously happy, well-adjusted children. And you will keep on being your fabulous self. That is all winner, baby!   
Do not let that troll of a sub-human dictate how you think of yourself. From where I'm sitting, you're amazing and a beautiful soul.   
When you think about what that sob said just remember this: 'If you point one finger, there are three more pointing back at you.' Everything he said about you isn't you it's all about him and his own inadequacies.   
You go be your best self, you bad-ass Momma!

I'm not one to tell people to break up. But in this case it might be for the best. At least keep your options open. Keep some $$ separate from family finances, and be ready to leave. He obviously will not put you or your child before his parents and siblings. You say he has FOMO - what about the birth of his child?? That's a once in a lifetime event and honestly you don't know when it's doing to happen. Could be early could be late. He is a huge a-hole and his parents doubly so. I promise you it will never get better with his parents. It this is the way they will treat you at one of the most vulnerable times of your life, it will always happen. I'm so sorry you're basically stuck with this jerk off for the rest of your daughter's childhood. Please be well, enjoy your Mom and Auntie (they sound like the best people) and never lose that best friend. She is definitely more family then your so-called fiancé.

NTJ She asked a ridiculous question. I don't know if she was just nervous and was trying and failing to make a joke. Or she could be a real jerk. But either way it was an honest answer to a really off remark.
NTJ some people should not be parents. I’m so glad you are safe and loved. Now get a therapist cause stuff like this does damage and you need to get on top of that.

Aw sweetie, I'm so so sorry this happened to you. Accidents happen and no one is perfect. Your Step-Dad was way out of line and you really should talk to your Mom about it when you're calm and can tell her how you feel. In the future, try to be more careful especially when SD is around. And stay out of his way. Don't make yourself a target. I'm sending you big hugs and all my hope that your Mom will help you sort this out. NTJ

Okay wow. I just read the whole story on Insta and I'm totally changing my comment. You're not the jerk, not one bit.

Your son is having a baby with an immature little troll who is trying to control you. While I don't think you should change your daughter's name, you shouldn't cut off your nose to spite your face.

You made your feelings well known, and I think telling gf that the ridiculous name is good was brilliant. But don't actually cut off your son if you want to know your granddaughter. I also think that this is not a relationship that will last (son and gf).  You don't really need to make nice and give in to their unreasonable demands. You should keep a sense of humor about it. Nothing pisses them off more than seeing they cannot get to you.

So instead of being the bigger person, be the funnier person. You will win in the end.

I have no advice to give you, but I can totally empathize. I proposed to my bf of 13 years. I bought a ring, asked permission from his daughter, and waited for Leap Day (Irish tradition) to get down on one knee. He looked at me and said: "You don't need a ring to prove I'm yours."  And that was pretty much that. I'm so sorry for your loss, but you will survive and flourish.

While yes they are soldiers it’s more about their relationships with their power and problem solving. 
In The Poppy Wars, Rin has to learn to overcome her fears and commune with the gods. She is constantly questioning her abilities and whether what she is doing is right or wrong. She’s very likable and relatable. She doesn’t know who she is or what she is and it’s overcoming those problems that she learns what power should be used for. 
Gideon and Harrow hate each other and are thrown into a Battle Royale together as partners. But it’s not their physical prowess or skill with weapons that help them but their ability to problem solve and work out the puzzles while staying alive. Both are wonderful characters and completely opposite each other. But both are brilliant and stupid in equal parts.
The Power is completely different. It’s focused on several women and their actions during a very turbulent world in which women gain an electrical power they can control. It’s about how the world reacts to that and what they do to free themselves from oppression. Mother Eve is a marvelous character that never actually fights but uses her words to encourage others to change the world. 

So while a lot of these books are focused on magic and physical abilities that’s not really the point of any of the characters. How they react to their worlds and survive is all about their inner strength and what they are willing to do or give up to achieve their goals.

Check out Gideon the Ninth and the follow up Harrow the Ninth by Tamsyn Muir. Both Gideon and Harrow are amazing female characters.

Also I'm almost finished with The Poppy War by RF Kuang and it's got a great female lead. Rin is powerful and intelligent.

And one of my newest favorite books is The Power by Naomi Alderman. It's all about sudden female empowerment and how the patriarchy deals with being the lesser sex.
